Subject: sudden spike in 5xx and token latency from our EU fleet

Hi Alex —

Starting around 08:45 UTC we saw a sudden jump in model token latency and a correlated rise in 5xx errors for requests routed from our EU customers (we're running calls through the dedicated endpoint you provisioned). P95 token latency jumped from ~120ms to 1.2s and 5xx rate climbed from 0.2% to ~6%.

We captured a short packet trace and some request IDs attached (network-trace-2027-07-14.pcap). Key observations from our side:
- errors look like upstream connection resets and a few DNS timeouts (NXDOMAIN/timeout) immediately before failures
- most failing requests appear to hit a proxy in front of the Redwood endpoint (based on TCP handshake IPs)

This is impacting our customer SLAs. Can you confirm if anything changed on Redwood's side (routing, model rollout, ipsec/peering) and advise next steps? We can hop on a call.

Thanks,
Carlos
Head of Platform Ops

Team / Carlos —

I ingested the pcap and cross-referenced our edge traces (console link: https://console.redwood.com/traces/helios/trace-77a2). Short summary:

Findings:
- We see a pattern of DNS queries for the Redwood edge hostname returning timeouts from one of the upstream resolvers in the EU transit path around 08:44–08:53 UTC. When DNS times out, the client attempts fallback which routes through an in-path proxy cluster we don't control (observed via src/dst ip changes in the pcap).
- Multiple connections show asymmetric routing: SYN arrives at our EU edge, but the SYN-ACK returns via a different egress IP (likely due to a transient route flap in the customer's provider or intermediate peering fabric). That explains the connection resets/late ACKs and token latency spikes.
- No signs of model-side CPU/GPU saturation on our nodes for the affected window; token service times on the server remain steady.

Immediate mitigations we can apply (recommend doing 1 + 2):
1) Short-term: Add a temporary DNS TTL override and force our edge hostname to prefer the stable resolver group (we can accomplish via a conservative TTL=30 override in the private zone for Helios; need Helios ops sign-off).
2) Short-term: Enable per-connection sticky routing on the EU edge for Helios traffic to reduce asymmetric path effects (config change on edge LB; low risk but requires minute outage for reload).
3) Mid-term: Work with Helios networking to validate their VPC peering advertisements — suspect a duplicate route announcement from a colo partner causing asymmetry.

I’ve attached a filtered pcap and an excerpt of tcpdump showing the SYN/SYN-ACK mismatch as a quick artifact.

Commands run (excerpt):
- tcpdump -r network-trace-2027-07-14.pcap 'tcp[tcpflags] & (tcp-syn|tcp-ack) != 0'
- netstat -rn | grep -E 'eu|0.0.0.0'

If Helios approves the DNS TTL/edge sticky routing I can push the changes immediately and monitor. Otherwise we can stand up an incident bridge.

— Sean Gallagher
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
